propositions.name: aberration_explained_by_emission
propositions.statement: On the emission theory, aberration of light is attributed to a composition of the velocity of light with the velocity of the earth in its orbit.
propositions.quote: The effect was attributed to a simple composition of the velocity of light with the velocity of the earth in its orbit.

propositions.name: emission_fails_water_telescope
propositions.statement: The emission theory failed to account for the fact that the aberration was unchanged when observations were made with a telescope filled with water.
propositions.quote: the aberration was unchanged when observations were made with a telescope filled with water

propositions.name: aberration_tangent_ratio
propositions.statement: On the emission theory the tangent of the angle of aberration is the ratio of the velocity of the earth to the velocity of light.
propositions.quote: the tangent of the angle of aberration is the ratio of the velocity of the earth to the velocity of light

propositions.name: velocity_light_water_three_fourths
propositions.statement: The velocity of light in water is three-fourths its velocity in a vacuum.

propositions.name: fresnel_ether_rest_outside_media
propositions.statement: According to Fresnel, the ether is at rest except in the interior of transparent media.
propositions.quote: the ether is supposed to be at rest except in the interior of transparent media

propositions.name: fresnel_ether_partial_drag_media
propositions.statement: According to Fresnel, in transparent media the ether moves with a velocity less than the velocity of the medium, in a fixed ratio.
propositions.quote: it is supposed to move with a velocity less than the velocity of the medium in the ratio

propositions.name: fizeau_confirms_partial_drag
propositions.statement: The hypothesis that the ether in media moves with less than the velocity of the medium must be considered fully proved by the experiment of Fizeau and by further confirmation.
propositions.quote: The second hypothesis, notwithstanding its seeming improbability, must be considered as fully proved, first, by the celebrated experiment of Fizeau , and secondly, by the ample confirmation of our own work.

propositions.name: ether_passes_through_metals

propositions.name: opaque_body_no_free_passage
